question: How many licensed traffic engineers must a road agency employ per 100 centerline miles to comply with the MUTCD?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The MUTCD does not specify any required number of licensed traffic engineers per centerline mile, and nothing in the provided evidence supports such a staffing ratio. The Manual sets uniform national criteria for traffic control devices themselves — not agency staffing levels — and it explicitly does not mandate that an engineer make the final decision to implement a traffic control solution; that responsibility rests with the agency having jurisdiction. Standards (mandatory): - The MUTCD "shall be recognized as the national standard for all traffic control devices installed on any street, highway, bikeway, or site roadway open to public travel" — a compliance obligation for devices, not for agency staffing. Support (explanatory): - The purpose of the MUTCD is "to establish uniform national criteria for the use of traffic control devices," not personnel requirements. - "The MUTCD does not mandate, and is not intending to imply, that an engineer must make the final decision whether to implement or execute the determination or advice of an engineer…" — the final decision rests with the agency having jurisdiction, after consultation with the engineer. - MUTCD principles are "developed for and used by individuals who are duly authorized and qualified to conduct traffic control device activities," without prescribing how many such individuals an agency must employ. Citations: - Section 1A.01 Support §1 (p.1) - Section 1B.01 Standard §1 (p.4) - Section 1D.03 Support §4 (p.32) - Section 1A.04 Support §1 (p.2)
